name: Portrait 1
short: Full-body portrait, head centered, shot at 1.5x from 4m away.
step_1: Camera height: Hold the camera at the subject's chest height.
step_2: 1.5x zoom: Shoot with 1.5x zoom to keep proportions natural.
step_3: 4m+ distance: Stand at least 4 metres away from the subject.
step_4: Head at center: Align the subject's head with the center of the frame.

name: Portrait 2
short: Portrait with the head on the top third line, shot at 2x.
step_1: Camera height: Hold the camera at the subject's chest height.
step_3: 4m+ distance: Stand at least 4 metres away from the subject.
step_4: Head on top 1/3 line: Align the head near the top third guide line.

name: Close Up
short: Half-body telephoto portrait at 3x for a flattering, flat background.
step_1: Camera height: Hold the camera at the subject's chest height.
step_3: 4m+ distance: Stand at least 4 metres away from the subject.
step_4: Head on top 1/3 line: Align the head near the top third guide line.

name: Side Chick
short: Off-center portrait that lets the scene tell the story, at 3–4x.
step_1: Camera height: Hold the camera at the subject's chest height.
step_3: 8m+ distance: Stand at least 8 metres away from the subject.
step_4: Head on top 1/3 line: Place the subject in the side box with the head near the top third line.

name: Travel Shot
short: Small subject at the bottom, big scenery above — the classic travel shot.
step_1: Front light: Face the scene with the sun behind you, ideally when shadows are minimal.
step_2: High 15°: Look down at a 15° angle, shooting from slightly higher than the subject.
step_3: 2–3x zoom: Stay 5–10 metres from the subject and use 2–3x zoom.
step_4: Subject placement: Place the subject small at the bottom center to emphasize the scenery.
tip: For two people, place them in the bottom corners facing each other.

name: One-Third
principle: Rule of thirds — subject in the lower third
short: Main scene in one third of the frame, sky in the other two.
step_1: Any direction: Works in any light direction; looks especially natural with side light.
step_2: Eye level: Set the camera at eye level and shoot.
step_3: 1.5x zoom: Stay at least 3 metres from the scene and use 1.5x zoom.
step_4: 1/3 placement: Place the main scene in the 1/3 area, separate it from its surroundings and line it up with the rule-of-thirds grid.
tip: Use horizontal lines or pillars, such as bridges, to separate the areas.

name: Two-Third
principle: Rule of thirds — subject fills two-thirds
short: Main subject fills two-thirds of the frame, with a strip for balance.
step_1: Any direction: Works in any light direction; looks especially natural with side light.
step_2: Eye level: Set the camera at eye level and shoot.
step_3: 1.5x zoom: Stay at least 3 metres from the scene and use 1.5x zoom.
step_4: 2/3 placement: Place the main scene in the 2/3 area, separate it from its surroundings and line it up with the rule-of-thirds grid.
tip: Use horizontal lines or pillar-like elements to separate the areas.

name: Vanishing Point
principle: Corner lines converging on the subject
short: Table edges converge on the subject for café and food shots.
step_1: Side light: Use natural light from a window-side seat.
step_2: High 45°: Shoot looking down at a 45° angle from above.
step_3: 2–4x zoom: Stay at least 2 metres from the scene and use 2–4x zoom.
step_4: Corner placement: Place the subject at the center, inside the square table corner.
tip: Clear everything except the background, the table and the subject.

name: One-Point Vertex
principle: Single subject on a grid intersection
short: One subject on a grid intersection, empty space opposite.
step_1: Side light: Use natural light from a window-side seat.
step_2: High 45°: Shoot looking down at a 45° angle from above.
step_3: 2–4x zoom: Stay at least 2 metres away and use 2–4x zoom.
step_4: Vertex placement: Place the subject diagonally at a grid intersection and leave the opposite side empty.
tip: This emphasizes the subject while conveying depth.

name: Two-Point Vertex
short: Two subjects on a diagonal — small at the bottom, large at the top.
step_1: Side light: Use natural light from a window-side seat.
step_2: High 45°: Shoot looking down at a 45° angle from above.
step_3: 2–4x zoom: Stay at least 2 metres away and use 2–4x zoom.
step_4: Vertex placement: Place the two subjects diagonally at grid intersections — the smaller one at the bottom, the larger one at the top.
tip: A diagonal arrangement adds visual tension.

name: Triangle 1
short: Three items as triangle points in the lower two-thirds.
step_1: Side light: Use natural light from a window-side seat.
step_2: High 45°: Shoot looking down at a 45° angle from above.
step_3: 2–4x zoom: Stay at least 2 metres from the scene and use 2–4x zoom.
step_4: Triangle placement: Arrange three subjects in the 2/3 area as the points of a triangle.
tip: Place smaller subjects at the bottom so the larger ones aren't blocked.

name: Triangle 2
short: A wide triangle of three items across the whole table.
step_1: Side light: Use natural light from a window-side seat.
step_2: High 45°: Shoot looking down at a 45° angle from above.
step_3: 2–4x zoom: Stay at least 2 metres from the scene and use 2–4x zoom.
step_4: Triangle placement: Arrange three subjects as the points of a triangle.
tip: Place smaller subjects at the bottom so the larger ones aren't blocked.

name: Aerial Triangle
principle: Top-down flat lay, items in a triangle
short: Top-down flat lay with the items arranged in a triangle.
step_1: Side light: Use natural light from a window-side seat.
step_2: Top-down (90°): Shoot straight down at a 90° vertical angle.
step_3: 1–2x zoom: Stay at least 1 metre from the subject and use 1–2x zoom.
step_4: Triangle placement: Place the table in the 2/3 area and arrange the items as triangle points.
tip: Clear everything except the background, the table and the subject.

name: One-Point Aerial
principle: Top-down flat lay, single hero dish
short: Top-down shot of one hero dish on the bottom grid line.
step_1: Side light: Use natural light from a window-side seat.
step_2: Top-down (90°): Shoot straight down at a 90° vertical angle.
step_3: 1–2x zoom: Stay at least 1 metre from the subject and use 1–2x zoom.
step_4: Subject placement: Align the table with the 2/3 area and place the subject at the center of the bottom grid line.
tip: Clear everything except the background, the table and the subject.
